notes: Read both units, full electric-grid context, all ten candidates and the review. Restored innovation as the mechanism driving institutional adaptation, named all U.S. economic referents, preserved temporal continuity in job creation, resolved the criticized situation to the three stated trends, and restored the historical naming contrast and the observation that many contemporary entrepreneurs are young.

claims.claim_text: People once called risk-takers, dreamers and small-business owners are now called entrepreneurs, independent contractors and small-business men and women.
Many contemporary U.S. entrepreneurs are characterized as too young to remember much of the twentieth century.
Their innovation drives improvement and forces established institutions to adapt or disappear.
As in the past, U.S. entrepreneurs, independent contractors and small-business owners still create most new U.S. jobs and form community commercial networks.
Their enterprise is characterized as the lifeblood of the U.S. economy but as weakening.
More U.S. businesses are closing than starting.
Older firms constitute an increasing share of U.S. companies.
The trends of net business closures, a growing share of older firms and slower productivity are judged inconsistent with starting a new growth era.
